html:
Steve Biko was a South African activist against apartheid who led the Black Consciousness Movement. His death in police custody in 1977 drew outrage around the world.

As a medical student in Durban he broke with the white-led student union and in 1968 helped found the South African Students' Organisation, for black students only. He argued that black people had to free their own minds from the sense of inferiority that white rule taught them, and lead their own struggle. His writings appeared under the name Frank Talk and were later collected as I Write What I Like.

The government banned him in 1973, confining him to his hometown and forbidding him to speak in public. His ideas still spread among the young people who led the Soweto uprising of 1976.

In August 1977 he was arrested. Police beat him badly, then drove him naked in the back of a truck over a thousand kilometres to Pretoria, where he died. His friend, the journalist Donald Woods, told the story abroad. In 1997 the policemen involved asked the Truth and Reconciliation Commission for amnesty, and were refused.
